entries.summary: createActivityEntry and activitySourceHash expose the single activity-entry serialization and source-fence hashing rules for durable adapters (#1113 A2a), including the existing resealed comparison projection.

Activity is an envelope log with bounded bytes, durable revision cursors, plaintext artifact entries, opaque sealed progress and retained source fences (#1113 A1). A1 is not deployable or independently mergeable: Postgres fails closed until A2, and canonical lifecycle/wake/union integration follows in A3-A5. Hosts must update log-entry readers and handle explicit cursor gaps. TimelineEvent and TimelineOrderKey order by store revision and within-entry offset; producer batchSeq/eventIndex remain provenance. TimelineMetadata.log supplies retained-row continuity; incremental events alone no longer infer missing log revisions.

POST /byok/activity and BYOK_ACTIVITY_PATH are removed (#1113). Device progress must use authenticated task.progress envelopes through POST /byok/messages; check operator inventory for external callers before release.

Pi subagents are the upstream pi-subagents 0.83.1 package loaded from its installed copy. Children run in-process or in pi-subagents' own runner and never re-enter the SDK, so the pi-subagent-print and pi-subagent-runner helper kinds and sdkDistributionManifest.piSubagentHelperKinds are removed; route only reservedHelperKinds through runSdkReservedHelperCommand. A single-file product's bundled re-entry, the sealed host and the keys-profile lane offer no subagent tool.

Tool-authorization approvals are Host-only by default (#1101): the control socket and byok-agent approve can no longer approve them; rejection is unaffected. Set DaemonConfig.localToolApproval: 'allow' to restore local tool-authorization approval.

Add task-level tool authorization rules and decision metadata. Claude MCP selectors use the shared trusted runtime identity observation within the callback deadline; custom ToolAuthorizationGate wrappers must forward the optional identity resolver to preserve MCP policy enforcement. In a toolAuthorization.fileScope session the auto gate also asks on every call for every tool outside the SDK read/write/edit file boundary (bash, MCP and extension tools), regardless of the built-in risk level; an allowWithoutAsking rule (exact tool name, command glob, or trusted MCP identity) is the only opt-out, a denial never executes and records the closed reason outside-file-scope, and the approval summary names the concrete command/tool identity.

Add the optional DaemonConfig.toolAuthorization.fileScope policy (#1061 slice 1): absent means inherit (unchanged behavior); home authorizes read+write of the canonical Agent home; workspaces adds explicit read/write roots (write implies read). It is legal only for auto tasks and requires agentHome; all + fileScope is rejected with invalid_file_scope. v1 admits it only on the ordinary Pi RPC lane on darwin/linux; other adapters, the prepared/durable lanes, memory-reader offers and Windows decline before claim with file_scope_unsupported and never fall back to an unscoped run. No wire, RuntimeCapabilities or launch-format change; scoped file tools and path enforcement ship in a later slice.

Validate every configured toolAuthorization.fileScope root after claim and before runtime start (#1061 slice 2): POSIX only, using Node built-ins lstat/realpath.native/stat dev+ino identity and O_NOFOLLOW. A missing root, root symlink, non-directory, changed identity or unsupported platform fails the claimed task non-retryably with a typed file_scope_unavailable/file_scope_unsupported reason instead of starting unscoped. Each denial and each scope adoption is recorded as a local file-scope DaemonEvent and daemon record (D12; allow is never recorded). Pi's native file tools, shell, MCP servers and extensions are still not scoped, so this is root validation, not file isolation; scoped file tools ship in a later slice.

Runtime version policies are pure data (#1103): an exact token or a component-boundary prefix, never a range, minimum, regular expression or semver dependency. A descriptor default, an adapter option and DaemonConfig.runtimes.<id>.versionPolicy are complete objects that replace one another wholesale through one resolver; default behavior is unchanged (Codex/Grok/Hermes still warn on an unqualified version, Claude/Pi still do not), and only a Host-configured block declines a runtime locally before claim with task.decline.code runtime_unavailable, runtimeUnavailable.cause version_blocked and retryable false. A descriptor default may not configure a block (invalid_version_policy / block_requires_host). Nothing to change unless a Host opts into a block.

task.decline carries a typed runtime_unavailable cause (#1103 B2a): the open code runtime_unavailable plus an optional runtimeUnavailable { cause, code? } nested field, an append-only cause vocabulary and one retryable default per cause. An older server strips the nested field and still records the open code; an unknown cause reads as unknown with the raw token. Existing decline reasons and retryable values are unchanged, and a runtime that a Host-configured version policy blocks now reports runtime_unavailable / version_blocked instead of the earlier runtime_version_blocked code.

conn.hello and PUT /byok/presence carry strip-safe version-policy and runtime-unavailable discovery data (#1103 B2b): runtimes[].versionPolicy and harnesses[].versionPolicy project the effective policy verdict as state plus the qualified token, and a top-level runtimeUnavailable[] names non-available runtimes/harnesses with the append-only cause and its retryable default. Presence keeps the built-in RuntimeId domain; harness policy travels only on conn.hello.harnesses[]. The runtime-unavailable-cause capability flag announces the typed cause. An older receiver drops every new field, and absence means unknown, never allow or available. Restart version changes are local-only (status/doctor/stderr) and never enter hello, presence, audit or a support bundle. Nothing to change unless a Host reads the new discovery fields.

RuntimeDetectResult (available), RuntimeObservation, DiagnosticsSnapshot.runtimes[] and Daemon.status().runtimes[] carry optional local-only executablePath and executableSource ('config' | 'path' | 'env') for the executable detection ran (#1103 O10). Control status adds the runtimeExecutables side channel so an older CLI's strict runtimes parser still accepts the array; status, runtimes and doctor print the executable. Neither field enters conn.hello, presence, audit.jsonl, DaemonRecord or a support bundle. Absence means unknown. Nothing to change unless a Host reads the new fields.

DaemonConfig has a generated, versioned JSON schema (daemon-config.schema.json beside the client package.json) and one validator for config files and createDaemon. Unknown fields are warnings, never rejected at runtime (Q4'); `byok-agent config check [--strict] [--json]` and checkDaemonConfig validate a config and report its effective values (store, Agent-home and scratch directories with the socket budget, MCP servers, memory helper, runtime isolation, tool-authorization mode). Daemon.status().config returns the same report. Each top-level DaemonConfig field is now a config:<field> manifest item. Nothing to change; run `byok-agent config check --strict` in CI to catch typos. AgentEgressConfig.policy is optional, as config files already wrote it (`"agentEgress": {}` selects the client default policy).

Daemon construction now validates DaemonConfig against the schema: a missing required field or a value of the wrong JSON type or literal throws DaemonConfigInvalidError (some fields were previously passed through unchecked), and the bin reports every config error at once. DaemonConfigFieldRemovedError gains a required `migration` (constructor third argument) pointing at the removed-field table; a removed field such as workspaceRoot keeps throwing it. Fix the reported fields; a Host that constructs DaemonConfigFieldRemovedError itself passes the migration anchor.

resolveHostLayout({ productId, productName, platform?, homeDir?, env? }) returns the recommended storeDir (the SDK default ~/.byok/<productId>, with its #493 scratch placement and socket-path budget), hostStorageRoot (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/<productName>, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/<productId>, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\<productName>), its agents directory and the service log directory. It is pure and throws HostLayoutInputError (code host_layout_input_invalid, with the field) on an input it cannot lay out. DaemonEffectiveConfig.directories gains logDir. Nothing to change; a Host that computes these directories itself can call the helper instead. Existing stores do not move.

The static DeviceStore.defaultDir(productId) is removed; it duplicated the default store path. The class is reachable through BlobClient and InstallSkillPacksOptions. The default storeDir is still <home>/.byok/<productId> and no store moves. A Host that called DeviceStore.defaultDir uses resolveHostLayout({ productId, productName }).storeDir. These same exports also contain private AuthManager declaration changes for the token-renewal minimum gap (#1114): a fast device clock or short server TTL no longer loops renewals and keychain writes. That renewal fix requires no additional Host action.

createByokCloud now refuses a port passed without its capability declared (capability_port_undeclared), as it already refused a capability declared without its port (#1096). Hosts that pass a port without declaring it must either declare the capability or stop passing the port. createByokServer no longer passes an E2EE member store and derives its declaration from its ports with the new capabilityDeclarationForPorts; createInMemoryByokCloud's default declaration is derived the same way. SqliteSchemaErrorCode drops SQLITE_MIGRATION_REFUSED, which only the removed E2EE KEM-floor check raised.

Read-only store compatibility precheck (#1102). Before switching versions, run the candidate build's inspectors to learn whether it accepts each local store, needs a new path and pairing (new-path-repair), or refuses it (rejected): inspectDaemonStores (@byok-sdk/client, journal and pi-durable replicas; also `byok-agent upgrade check --store [--json]`, exit 2 when a store would be refused), inspectSqliteStore (@byok-sdk/server) and inspectProviderProfileStore (@byok-sdk/keys), all returning the StoreCompatibility type from @byok-sdk/core. Each one opens only a private temporary copy of the files.

One per-device rate budget now covers every authenticated device route, and every Host route body is bounded (#1118). InboundRateLimiter.consume(tenant, deviceId, unit, count) takes a RateLimitUnit and a count and returns a RateLimitDecision ({ allowed: true } or { allowed: false, retryAfterMs }) instead of a boolean; a custom limiter must adopt the new signature (there is no boolean form). Every authenticated device route except POST /byok/messages spends one 'request' unit, including each GET /byok/events poll, presence publishes and skill-pack reads. POST /byok/messages charges its whole batch ('envelope', count = batch length) as one admission before any envelope applies, so a refused batch applies nothing; handleInboundEnvelope no longer consults the limiter and InboundResult/InboundOutcome have no rate_limited member. A token bucket admits while it holds one token and then charges the whole count, so a batch larger than the burst overdraws it and the next admission waits for the debt (the embedded server's RateLimiter.consume(key, cost) does this). A refusal answers 429 { error: 'rate limit exceeded' } with Retry-After in whole seconds (POST /byok/messages included). JSON device routes that read their body without a ceiling now answer 413 { error: 'request body too large' } above their own limit: presence = presenceDetailMaxBytes + 64 KiB, activity = activityMaxBytes + 16 KiB, board claim/status 4 KiB, POST /byok/blobs and both projection/preparation completions 16 KiB. The presigned blob PUT allocates its one buffer on the first arriving byte and holds at most one upload per blob: a concurrent PUT of the same blob answers 409 { error: 'upload_in_progress' } (a stable code; retry after the first finishes). BlobContentProxy gains a required claimUpload(blobId): Promise<(() => void) | undefined>; a custom proxy must return a release function, or undefined while an upload of that blob is in flight, and keep claims in process memory. Embedded server: rateLimit now budgets route requests too, so size burst for a connect (conn.hello + presence) plus polls; stats().envelopesIn still counts envelopes only, stats().rateLimitEvents counts refused requests as well.

createPostgresCloudStores requires a rateLimit option and composes a per-process token bucket instead of AllowAllRateLimiter (#1118); there is no unlimited Postgres composition. Pass rateLimit: { tokensPerSecond, burst, maxTrackedDevices? } (the embedded server's defaults are 50/s and burst 100; maxTrackedDevices defaults to 100,000, least recently used buckets are dropped beyond it). Each envelope and each authenticated device route request except POST /byok/messages spends one token; a refusal answers 429 with Retry-After. The budget is per process: N replicas admit up to N times the configured rate, so keep an edge limiter when you need one global budget.

The task.fail reason schema now transforms with boundFailureReason (#1124): createEnvelope and every decode redact credentials (Authorization/Bearer values, provider key shapes, *KEY/*TOKEN/*SECRET/*PASSWORD* assignments, URL userinfo) and cap the reason at TASK_FAIL_REASON_MAX_BYTES UTF-8 bytes with a truncation marker. A longer reason is truncated, never refused, and no field is removed; machine-readable failure stays in task.fail.failure. Breaking because decode no longer returns such a reason verbatim: a Host that parsed the stderr tail out of reason must read the local daemon diagnostics instead, and a terminal receipt stored before this release whose reason is unbounded is not rewritten and no longer re-encodes byte-for-byte, so settle in-flight task terminals before upgrading the cloud.

Every retention class declares a bound (#1105). The SDK now expires Pi's own session files in DaemonConfig.piByokLauncher.sessionDir (class pi-session-dir, 31 days by last write) and -task- terminal evidence in each Agent home (class terminal-evidence, 30 days); both moved from ProtectedClassId to ExpiringClassId, and the never-populated retired-namespace class is gone. New protected class runtime-session-external registers runtime session records outside the Agent home. storage.retention.ttlMs['pi-session-dir'] must be at least ttlMs['session-ledger'] plus one day, else LocalStorageConfigError. A Host that trimmed the Pi session folder itself deletes that code; a Host that raised the session-ledger TTL raises the pi-session-dir TTL too.

Prepared operations that own swept session data expose acquireSessionLease. TaskRunner acquires it before validating a resume handoff and passes the exact local RuntimeSessionLease to start; callers retain it until confirmed disposal. Pi admission and actual child writer gates coordinate shared session directories, including parent crashes and native session replacement.

Renewal halts as revoked at once only on the typed /byok/challenge or /byok/token 401 body {error, code: 'device_not_registered'}, which the reference handlers now send for an unknown or revoked device. Any other 401 backs off, rechecks once, and halts only if the recheck is rejected too. Every OS keychain command has a deadline and is killed on timeout or daemon stop (DeviceCredentialCommandAbortedError); DeviceCredentialBackend methods take an optional AbortSignal that an injected backend should honor (#1117). A custom server without the typed body still halts, after the one recheck.

A storeDir only uses the OS enrollment its own pair-time device.json names (#1094). Startup, status, identity and the stored signer no longer self-heal a missing or different device.json from the productId-keyed OS entry: they throw DeviceStoreBindingMismatchError (code device_store_not_bound), and start halts as the new DaemonHaltReason 'store_not_bound'. Pairing refuses while the OS entry holds an enrollment this storeDir did not pair, unless Daemon.pair(code, { replaceOtherStore: true }) / byok-agent pair --replace-other-store. Unpair from such a store fails closed. Replacement pairing stages its durable retry key beside the current enrollment in the same bounded OS entry; failures retain the prior authority, same-enrollment renewal preserves the attempt, and successful authenticated promotion consumes it. Injected DeviceCredentialBackend implementations must preserve that staging contract. Older clients reject the staged private state; the 2400-byte bound is unchanged.

Pair and token responses carry expiresIn, the access token lifetime in seconds. A device computes its token expiry from its own receipt time plus expiresIn and no longer from expiresAt or refreshHint, so a device clock that is off by hours keeps the normal renewal schedule. A device refuses a pair or token response without expiresIn with AuthResponseInvalidError, whose route now includes 'pair'. Upgrade the Host before its devices; the Host keeps sending expiresAt and refreshHint for devices on earlier releases.

Automatic maintenance now reaps mailbox dead letters once mailboxDeadLetterRetentionMs (default 30 days) has passed after they expired, but keeps each device's highest-seq dead letter as the recoverableFrom floor. RetentionPolicy gains mailboxDeadLetterRetentionMs, so a Host that passes a complete policy must add it. A custom MailboxStore receives the new required reapDeadLettersBefore input in collectExpired and must reap the same way. discardDeadLetter refuses the floor row with cleanup_dead_letter_is_recovery_floor. Migration 0031 adds the tenant_retention_policy column with the 30-day default and replaces outbox_tenant_bytes_idx with a pending-only partial index. Migration 0034 replaces activity_tail with an empty durable activity log in place: stop old writers/readers, explicitly accept loss of bounded pre-cutover activity history, reject old cursors with a gap, and drop the old table; no row conversion or dual read. TENANT_ERASURE_TABLES replaces activity_tail with activity_log_entry/activity_log_head, affecting Hosts that iterate the table list.

The Agent memory contract shared by the device and the Host (AgentMemoryFile, AgentMemorySnapshot, AgentMemoryExport, AgentMemoryProjectionPort, AgentMemoryIntentFetchInput, AgentMemoryIntentTransport, validateAgentMemoryPath, AgentMemoryError, AgentMemoryValidationError) moved from @byok-sdk/client and @byok-sdk/client/agent-memory to the new zod-free @byok-sdk/protocol/agent-memory entry, its only definition (#1106). Import these names from @byok-sdk/protocol/agent-memory; client no longer exports them. The error classes now have one runtime definition, so instanceof AgentMemoryError holds across client entries.

The K4 Host execution core (FIFO, ledger, routines, transitions, schedule, submit, model, sealed routine, Host memory page and restore) is published as @byok-sdk/server/execution-core, with hash and canonical in the Worker-safe @byok-sdk/server/execution-core/canonical entry (#1106). examples/host-execution-core is now a demo that composes these entries; its package exports only ./test-support. A Host that vendored K4 deletes the copy and its provenance check and imports the subpaths; the Host ledger file is kept. MemoryBlockedError is newly exported. K8 imports the published entries; its own vendoring is unchanged.

doctor reports the device clock skew measured from the server Date header of the last pair or token response, as a new clock-skew check and a clockSkew snapshot field; it warns beyond 60 s, the Host's default device-proof window. PairResponse.expiresIn is registered as a strip-safe HTTP wire addition. No Host action.

POST /byok/messages decodes each entry on its own (#1121). An entry that is not a valid Envelope is answered rejected with reason payload_invalid and the rest of the batch applies; only a broken frame (not { messages: [...] }, an entry whose v is not this wire major, an entry without a UUID id, or more than 256 entries) still fails the whole request with 400. MessagesSendRequestSchema now validates that frame only: its messages entries are typed { v, id } plus unvalidated fields, so code that read decoded envelopes from it must decode each entry with parseMessage. A terminal whose task already holds a stored receipt the Host cannot read back is refused for that envelope with state_conflict (internal reason terminal_receipt_not_canonical in INBOUND_REFUSAL_REASONS) instead of a 500 for the batch. Devices need no change: a rejected outcome was already final for them.

Device -> Host vocabularies a newer device may extend are open (#1121): task.fail.failure.class, task.decline.code and a denied agent.content.receipt reason accept any well-formed token ([a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}) this version does not know and keep it verbatim, so the report is recorded instead of rejected; a failure class it does not know may carry extra fields, which are kept too. The wire types widen accordingly (TaskFailure, the decline code and the denial reason admit unrecognized tokens). Hosts read them with readTaskFailure and readDeclineCode: a value this version does not know reads as class/code 'unknown' with the raw token in reportedClass/reportedCode. Cloud TerminalResult and embedded TaskResult now carry these readings: failure is a TaskFailureReading, code is a TaskDeclineCodeReading code, and a new reportedCode field holds an unknown code's raw token. Switch on failure.class and code as before and handle 'unknown'.

Automatic maintenance gains a tasks step (#1120), run after mailbox: a terminal task is archived terminalTaskArchiveMs (default 90 days, at least mailboxUnackedRetentionMs + mailboxDeadLetterRetentionMs) after it ended. In one store transaction its bodies become redaction tombstones, its ephemeral rows and sealed-task object references go and archived_at is set; then its board item is removed and settle deletes any rows a custom store keeps outside that transaction (archived tasks leave the board). The task row and tombstoned receipts stay as the replay fence until tenant deletion (about 1.2 KB per task on Postgres). Content reads answer task_content_redacted; status reads stay. Device replays answer as before the archive: a claim or daemon_interrupted recovery report, which needs the now-tombstoned offer, is answered from the task's claim snapshot or, for an unclaimed task, from an exact match of its terminal receipt. An explicitly redacted task still refuses both, as before. RetentionPolicy gains terminalTaskArchiveMs, so a Host passing a complete policy adds it. CloudStores gains the required taskArchive port and BoardStore gains remove (idempotent): a custom store implements both. TaskAttempt gains archivedAt. Migration 0032 adds the policy column (NOT NULL, no default: stop policy writers from before #1120 first) backfilled to max(90 days, unacked + dead-letter windows) with every other window kept, refuses before any change a stored policy whose windows the application would reject or whose window sum exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and adds the task archive columns and backfills archive_after once from COALESCE(terminal_at, updated_at) for terminal rows; count terminal rows first, see the runbook. Embedded SQLite files add the columns and the same backfill on open.

ByokCloudOptions.proofReceiptRetention is required (#1120): every deployment prunes used device-proof request ids, so the proofReceipts maintenance step never reports not-configured. A Host that omitted it passes its ProofReceiptRetentionAuthority (Postgres: PostgresProofReceiptRetentionAuthority; in-memory compositions now carry InMemoryProofReceiptRetentionAuthority as proofReceiptAuthority).

The Postgres mailbox wake LISTEN connection enables TCP keepalive and probes itself every probeIntervalMs (default 30 s); a probe that is not observed reconnects and reports a MailboxWakeProbeMissedError through onError (#1120). No Host change is needed.

Revoking a device, or superseding it when its machine re-pairs, now settles it in the same store transaction (#1119): its unfinished tasks become cancelled with terminalCause device_revoked or device_superseded, and its pending mailbox rows become expired, freeing their quota (no row is deleted and nothing returns to pending). New ByokCloud.abandonTask(tenant, taskId, cause) (and ByokServer.tasks.abandon / TaskHandle.abandon) settles one task the same way with a TASK_ABANDON_CAUSES cause; rows of a device that is still registered stay pending for it to ack, and its later reports for the task are refused (task_settled_by_cloud, a non-halting state_conflict). abandonTask sends nothing to a device, so it does not stop a live runtime; cancelTask does. readTaskResult reports a cloud-settled task from its attempt row. Custom stores must implement MailboxStore.expirePending and TaskCancellationStore.abandon and settle on revoke/register; InMemoryDeviceDirectory, InMemoryTaskCancellationStore and the Postgres directory take new constructor arguments. On the device, a halted or crashed run now ends its active tasks itself (journaling each task.fail for the next start) and its ended connection queues nothing more.

A daemon runs at most DaemonConfig.maxConcurrentTasks tasks at once (default 8; a positive safe integer, no uncapped value), counted across every Agent home and runtime (#1121). Before, the device-wide count was unbounded. An offer over the cap is declined retryably before the claim, with no decline code, so a Host of any version accepts the decline. DaemonConfig.defaultMaxDurationMs (optional) is the wall-clock limit for a task whose offer carries no limits.maxDurationMs. While the Host is unreachable, the outbound queue keeps at most 8 MiB of task.progress and agent.message.draft envelopes and drops the oldest beyond that; terminals, claims, starts and approval requests are never dropped, and OutboundStatus.droppedEphemeral counts the drops. A Host that dispatches more than 8 concurrent tasks to one device sets maxConcurrentTasks to its own number.

An unreadable delivery cursor file (torn, hand-edited, or not a nonnegative integer) no longer reads as a missing cursor (#1121). Startup halts with the new DaemonHaltReason 'cursor_unreadable'. The operator resets it with byok-agent doctor --repair reset-cursor --yes, or resetDeviceCursor(config, { confirmed: true }) in an embedded host: the cursor becomes 0 and the next start replays what the server retains; journaled offers are matched by id and ended tasks are not redelivered. An expired history still halts replay_cursor_too_old. Handle 'cursor_unreadable' wherever you switch on DaemonHaltReason.

A single-file Host (single-file ESM, single-file CommonJS or a Node SEA) has an SDK build helper in @byok-sdk/client/packaging (#1104): the byokSdkPackaging esbuild plugin (no esbuild dependency) sets each format's module require or import.meta.url and fails the build on any empty import.meta, SDK files included, except three reviewed third-party sites (sdkBundleImportMetaExemptions); copySdkPackagingAssets copies the Pi runtime and native assets one target ships, in sdkPackagingAssetLayout. bundledSdkHelperHost() is the sdkHelperHost of the running bundle or SEA. sdkDistributionManifest adds nodeEngine, a role for every published bin (bins) and the formats. In a CommonJS or SEA bundle, PDF reads lose unpdf's standard font and CMap defaults, as before. Nothing changes for a Host that does not use them.

Runtimes no longer inherit the daemon's process.env (#1095). Every adapter builds its children's environment under a RuntimeEnvironmentPolicy (constructor option runtimeEnvironment; createDaemon passes DaemonConfig.runtimeEnvironment, createDaemonWithAdapters rejects that field). The default base is the user's login-shell snapshot, captured once per process with the account's login shell (read from the account database by uid, never $SHELL; a failed lookup is the new ServiceEnvironmentUnavailableCode account-shell-unavailable) from a closed seed and a fixed PATH, so CLIs on the user's shell PATH are found in embedded use too; 'allowlist' is the strict mode over the live environment; 'pass' names live variables a Host sets. CLAUDECODE and BYOK_* are always removed, NO_PROXY/no_proxy gain 127.0.0.1 and localhost, and Claude drops the shell's ANTHROPIC_*, Bedrock/Vertex switches and OAuth token when pass supplies a provider. A failed capture fails closed: RuntimeEnvironmentUnavailableError, detection refused with the new reason runtime_environment_unavailable and its code (RuntimeObservation.code), offers declined. win32 uses the session baseline names (ServiceEnvironmentStatus source 'windows-session'). RuntimeAdapter gains the required runtimeEnvironment(); custom adapters implement it with buildRuntimeEnvironment. Prepared input bindings use the Pi adapter's environment, so a daemon without a Pi adapter refuses them (detail pi_runtime_unconfigured). The adapters entry's buildRuntimeEnv is removed; the testing fake defaults to the allowlist environment. A Host whose runtime needs a variable it set itself lists the name in pass.

The path-mutation gate (#1149), which SDK processes on one machine use to exclude each other from a store, an Agent home, a skill-pack store or a Pi session, is now an OS lock owned by one open handle: an O_EXLOCK open of /tmp/byok-pm-<uid>/<identity>.lock on macOS, an abstract unix socket on Linux, a named pipe on Windows as before. The OS frees it when its holder exits, and no SDK process removes another's gate. Releases up to 0.31 used unix socket files under /tmp/byok-pm-<uid>, which do not exclude the new locks on macOS and Linux. Migration: before upgrading any participant, stop every SDK process that shares a protected target with it or takes part in the same pathless Pi rebinding barrier (the daemon, the CLI, an App that embeds the SDK, the adapters, the actual Pi writer, the sweeper and relocation), for every store involved, including other stores that share a Pi session directory, an Agent home root or a skill-pack store, and start them again only once all of them run the new release; upgrading one store while another participant still runs 0.31 or earlier is not supported. Windows is unaffected. The gates coordinate only processes (the daemon, the adapters, the actual Pi writer, the sweeper and relocation) that run as the same UID, in the same Linux network namespace, and reach each protected target (store, Agent home root, skill-pack store, Pi session directory) through a consistent canonical path; the pathless Pi rebinding barrier is shared per UID and network namespace. Processes in different network namespaces do not exclude each other: each namespace must use disjoint stores and disjoint protected targets, with no Agent home root, skill-pack store or Pi session directory shared across namespaces.

Service units are one library API for the CLI and embedded Hosts (#1097). ServiceDefinition requires storeDir and owner; agentServiceDefinition builds the byok-agent definition that `byok-agent install` uses. A unit names only a stable launcher (<storeDir>/service/<name>.launcher.sh on macOS/Linux; the installed WinSW <name>.exe on Windows) and carries an SDK marker. ServiceLifecycle gains inspect() (absent/exact/repairable/foreign) and repair(); status() adds unit and logs. A foreign (marker-less) unit is never changed: install/repair/uninstall/start/stop throw ServiceUnitError service_unit_unmarked unless install({ replaceUnmarked: true }) (CLI --replace-unmarked). ServiceInstallOptions.program is removed; pass the program in the definition. One lifecycle owner per store (claim/read/releaseServiceLifecycleOwner, lifecycle_owner_conflict); every owner-record change, and install/repair/uninstall for their whole run, holds a cross-process service-lifecycle gate (one per user, one per machine on Windows; relocation takes it before its store gates), and a held gate fails at once with lifecycle_owner_busy. Exit-code contract EXIT_CODE_CONTRACT: only exit 0 stops a service; systemd units now use Restart=always with RestartPreventExitStatus=0. Under --service the daemon writes its own rotated <logDir>/daemon.log (DAEMON_LOG_LIMITS); the redirect files are renamed service-stdout.log/service-stderr.log and bounded (SERVICE_REDIRECT_LIMITS); WinSW rolls by size. generateLaunchdPlist/generateSystemdUnit take launcherPath and workingDirectory instead of program. DiagnosticsSnapshot and support bundles gain log sizes (no paths); exportDeviceSupportBundle and `support-bundle` refuse an output inside the store. Migration: a unit installed by 0.31 or earlier has no marker; replace it once with `byok-agent install --replace-unmarked`, or remove it with the 0.31 CLI's `uninstall` first. A Host that built ServiceDefinition adds storeDir and owner.

A byok-agent config file can set the toolAuthorization policy ({ default, byRuntime, rules }) and the isolation options of the adapters createDaemon builds (runtimes.pi/claude/codex). The policy becomes the one per-offer resolver at construction; an unknown byRuntime key, or auto on a runtime without toolAuthorizationAuto, is a DaemonConfigInvalidError. createDaemonWithAdapters rejects runtimes. The effective report gains toolAuthorization mode static with the resolved per-runtime modes.

DaemonConfig.toolAuthorization is one policy document, { default, byRuntime?, rules? }, for both a config file and an embedded Host; the function-or-object union is gone. StaticToolAuthorization, staticToolAuthorizationMode, staticToolAuthorizationResolver and ToolAuthorizationResolver are removed, and ToolAuthorizationPolicy no longer has the { mode } spelling (a single mode is { default: mode }). Replace a function resolver with the policy object; per-runtime modes move to byRuntime and rules keep their reviewed precedence and admission rules. An invalid policy (a bad rule, selector, glob or fileScope) now throws DaemonConfigInvalidError (code daemon_config_invalid) at daemon construction, with the issue path toolAuthorization or toolAuthorization.fileScope (code invalid_file_scope), instead of a plain TypeError or FileScopePolicyError; checkDaemonConfig reports the same issue. Offers are no longer declined with tool_authorization_unresolved. Catch DaemonConfigInvalidError where a Host caught the TypeError.

Each bundled adapter declares its capability matrix in one constant: toolAuthorizationAuto, durablePi, preparedLane and isolation (userContext, userMcpServers, sessionPersistence), next to steer, resume, messageDraft and mcpToolsets. The daemon reports it per runtime in conn.hello runtimes[]/harnesses[] and task.claim, and in presence runtimes[].capabilities, which the cloud stores and returns from presence reads; all of it is strip-safe and optional, and a field an older daemon omits is unknown. docs/adapter-capabilities.md's matrix table is generated from the same constants. No Host action; a Host may read presence runtimes[].capabilities before dispatch, for example to choose all instead of auto.

Versioned service installs and upgrades (#1097). createServiceInstallation installs a Host-verified payload (a directory plus byok-payload.json listing each file's SHA-256) under a Host-owned install root as versions/<id> with current and previous pointers, so the unit and launcher never change. upgrade() stops the service, runs the candidate's store precheck and stops before the switch on new-path-repair or rejected (ServiceInstallationError store_repair_required / store_rejected, with the verdicts), snapshots every listed store, switches, and restores the old version and its snapshot together when the new one fails its health check (health_check_failed). rollback(), recover() for an interrupted switch, uninstall() and upgrade-receipt.json complete it; agentServiceInstallation is the byok-agent payload's installation. The CLI adds install --payload <dir> --install-root <dir> and upgrade apply <dir> | rollback | recover | status. A service installed without a payload is unchanged.

A retired device's mailbox stream is now closed (#1160). Revoking or superseding a device closes its stream in the retirement's transaction, and every later append for that device id is refused, whatever its admission and even for a known messageId: core raises mailbox_stream_closed (MailboxStreamClosedError, with deviceId and closeCause), and ByokCloud raises device_retired (DeviceRetiredError, with deviceId and retirementCause). Before, a writer whose check ran before the retirement (offers, agent controls, scope-key notices, approve/reject, steer, inbound acks, dead-letter replay) could still commit a pending row for the retired device. An offer refused this way settles its attempt cancelled with the retirement cause in the same call and names its taskId; a scope-key notice skips a recipient retired after the list was read; a /byok/messages batch whose reply is refused answers 401. Registering the same device id again reopens the stream; rows, cursor, seq and recoverableFrom are kept. Custom stores must implement MailboxStore.closeStream and reopenStream, refuse appends on a closed stream, and close on revoke and supersede and reopen on register; MailboxStore.expirePending no longer takes seqs 'all'. Postgres: migration 0033 adds device_stream.closed_at and closed_cause and closes, as device_revoked, the stream of every device whose row is already gone (a supersede before the upgrade reads as a revoke); the migration writes the tombstone and does not expire those pending rows, which the dead-letter retention collects. Embedded SQLite: a schema 6 file is upgraded in place to 7 when it opens, with the same backfill, keeping its pairings and rows; older versions are refused as before, and a v7 file cannot be opened by an earlier build.
